name: Jochberg
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village at the end of the Jochbergtal valley, featuring the Kitzbühel ski area and the scenic Reschenpass road.
beschreibung:
Overview

Jochberg is situated at an elevation of 923 metres in the Leukental Valley within the Kitzbühel Alps, in the district of Kitzbühel, roughly eight kilometres south of the world-famous alpine resort of Kitzbühel. Stretching along the Kitzbüheler Ache river up to the Pass Thurn (1,274 m)—the historic mountain pass leading into Salzburg's Pinzgau region—the village is home to around 1,550 inhabitants across a sprawling area of nearly 88 square kilometres. In delightful contrast to the bustling glamour of its northern neighbour, Jochberg has carefully preserved its down-to-earth rural charm. Flanked by the rolling grassy peaks of the Kitzbühel Alps and the rugged northern ramparts of the High Tauern, the town is celebrated for its pristine spring waters, prehistoric copper mining legacy, and seamless connection to the vast KitzSki domain.

History

Mining and settlement in Jochberg date back to prehistoric times: Around 1000 BC during the Bronze Age, miners were already extracting and smelting copper ores high on the Kelchalpe pasture. The locality was first recorded in 1073 when Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV confirmed estates in Iochperch belonging to the Bavarian monastery of Rott. Copper mining experienced a major resurgence in the 15th century, with the famed Holy Ghost Adit opened around 1600 and the mining network later becoming known as the Kupferplatte. Mining ceased in 1926, before being revitalised as a show mine in 1990 by local water researcher Johann Grander. The Rococo Parish and Pilgrimage Church of St. Wolfgang was built between 1748 and 1752 by master architect Kassian Singer. Beneath its choir emerges the renowned St. Wolfgang Spring, a healing water source venerated since the 16th century for eye and joint ailments.

Getting There

Jochberg boasts convenient regional transport links. Motorists travelling from the north take the Inntal Motorway A12 to Kufstein-Süd or Wörgl-Ost, continuing past Kitzbühel along the B161 Pass Thurn federal road for just ten minutes straight into Jochberg. From the south (Salzburg, East Tyrol), the well-maintained B161 leads directly over the Pass Thurn from Mittersill. Rail passengers arrive at Kitzbühel Central Station, served regularly by high-speed Railjet, Intercity, and Eurocity trains. Outside the station, regional bus route 4010 operates frequent daily services directly to Jochberg village centre and the Wagstättbahn gondola terminal.

Tips

A journey deep into the Kupferplatte show mine is an unforgettable family highlight: An authentic electric mine train carries passengers 600 metres underground into the historic tunnels to explore miners' lore and the subterranean Stephanie Spring. In winter, the Wagstättbahn gondola in the village centre provides direct access into the world-class KitzSki area with 233 kilometres of slopes, connecting seamlessly to the iconic 3S gondola towards Hahnenkamm. Nature lovers should hike to the roaring 85-metre Sintersbach Waterfall along a romantic circular forest trail, stopping at the rustic Wildalm alpine hut. On hot summer days, unwind at the tranquil forest swimming pool (Waldschwimmbad), fed with revitalised local spring water.
